title: Add Kubernetes sidecar RAG starter with typed tool contracts and local retriever emulator
author: Aisha Malik
description:
This PR adds a new opinionated quickstart that demonstrates a production-oriented RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) deployment pattern using a lightweight k8s sidecar retriever combined with a typed tool-contract approach for tool-calling. Goals: 1) provide an approachable example for teams that want to separate retrieval from model execution without running an external managed vector DB; 2) show how to declare explicit JSON schemas for tools and use the Typescript/py SDK helpers to validate contracts at runtime; 3) include a local retriever emulator that runs as a sidecar in the pod so the quickstart is fully runnable on a developer laptop or in a CI test cluster. The quickstart includes: - A README-guided walk-through that covers architecture, deployment steps (kubectl / kind / k3d), and troubleshooting. - A small Python microservice (fastapi) that hosts the app logic and uses the Redwood SDK to call the hosted API or a local Private deployment via env configs. - A Go-based sidecar retriever that emulates a vector DB (in-memory) and exposes a simple HTTP search API with configurable latency profiles for testing SLOs and cache behavior. - Typed tool contracts (JSON Schema and TypeScript types) for two tools: 'document_fetch' and 'source_extractor'. The SDK examples show schema validations, error handling, and graceful fallback to a cached result. - GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs lint, unit tests, and a kind-based end-to-end smoke test. - Example alerting rules and SLO snippets for the Redwood Console based on token cost and tail latency. Why this is different from existing quickstarts: most RAG examples target hosted vector services or focus on agent/single-process orchestrators. This quickstart is intentionally ops-oriented: it teaches patterns for sidecar retrieval, typed tool contracts, and localizable emulation of production latency profiles so platform and infra teams can iterate without incurring DB costs. Checklist:
- [x] Add starter code for python app and go sidecar
- [x] Add README and architecture diagram (SVG)
- [x] Add types and schema examples
- [x] Add CI workflow and smoke test
- [x] Add console SLO examples
Notes: The retriever emulator is explicitly not intended for production persistence. It is annotated in the README with migration guidance to a cloud vector DB or Redwood Dedicated-backed persistent retriever. Related Linear: ENG-4821 tracks the sidecar pattern validation, PM-129 requested the typed contracts feature.
